stories.headline: Google Releases Gemma 4, Its Most Capable Open Model Family, Under Apache 2.0 License

key_facts.fact: Gemma 4 ships in four sizes: Effective 2B, Effective 4B, 26B Mixture of Experts, and 31B Dense, all built from the same research and technology as Gemini 3.
The 31B Dense model ranks #3 and the 26B MoE ranks #6 among open models on the Arena AI text leaderboard, outperforming models 20x their size.
Gemma 4 is released under Apache 2.0 license for the first time, a shift from previous restrictive terms that allows full commercial use and developer flexibility.
The larger models offer 256K context windows, edge models support 128K, and all models natively process images and video; E2B and E4B also support native audio input.
The 26B MoE activates only 3.8 billion of its total parameters during inference for fast tokens-per-second, while the 31B Dense maximizes raw quality for fine-tuning.
Developers have downloaded Gemma models over 400 million times since the first generation, building over 100,000 variants.

stories.headline: Microsoft Launches Three In-House AI Models: MAI-Transcribe-1, MAI-Voice-1, and MAI-Image-2

key_facts.fact: MAI-Transcribe-1 achieves 3.8% average Word Error Rate on FLEURS across top 25 languages, beating OpenAI's Whisper-large-v3 on all 25 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash on 22 of 25.
MAI-Voice-1 generates 60 seconds of audio in one second and supports custom voice creation from just a few seconds of audio, priced at $22 per 1M characters.
MAI-Image-2 debuted as a top-3 model family on the Arena.ai leaderboard and delivers at least 2x faster generation times, with WPP building at scale.
Teams of fewer than 10 engineers built each model, with Suleyman saying gains came from model architecture and data rather than headcount.
Suleyman declared Microsoft 'a top three lab just under OpenAI and Gemini' and said the models run on half the GPUs of competitors.
MAI-Transcribe-1 is priced at $0.36/hour, MAI-Image-2 at $5/1M input tokens and $33/1M image output tokens, deliberately undercutting AWS and Google Cloud.

stories.headline: Anthropic Acquires Biotech AI Startup Coefficient Bio for ~$400M in Stock

key_facts.fact: Anthropic acquired Coefficient Bio, a stealth New York-based biotech AI startup, in a stock deal valued at just over $400 million.
The startup was founded roughly eight months ago with fewer than 10 people, mostly former Genentech computational biology researchers from its Prescient Design unit.
Coefficient Bio had built a platform enabling AI to carry out biotech tasks including drafting drug R&D plans, managing clinical regulatory strategies, and discovering new drug candidates.
The team joins Anthropic's Healthcare Life Sciences group led by Eric Kauderer-Abrams, who laid out a roadmap to make Claude 'hands down the best model for everything in biology.'
Against Anthropic's $380 billion post-money valuation from its February Series G, the acquisition represents roughly 0.1% dilution.

stories.headline: Cursor Launches Cursor 3, an Agent-First Coding Workspace With $2B ARR and 1M Daily Users

key_facts.fact: Cursor 3 is a unified agent-first workspace built from scratch, merging Ask, Edit, and Agent modes into a single session without losing context history.
Cursor has reached $2.0 billion in annualized revenue with over 1 million daily active users, following a $2.3 billion Series D at a $29.3 billion valuation.
The new Agent mode executes fully autonomous tasks: running shell commands, large-scale refactoring, and web searches without manual prompting.
Cursor 3 supports seamless handoff between local and cloud agents, with cloud agents producing demos and screenshots for verification.
Cursor ships Composer 2, an in-house model it claims matches GPT-5.4 on coding benchmarks at one-tenth the cost, though Moonshot AI alleges it uses their Kimi K2.5 model without license compliance.

stories.headline: Anthropic Finds 171 Emotion-Like Vectors in Claude That Causally Drive Safety-Relevant Behavior

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's interpretability team extracted 171 identifiable emotion-like internal states from Claude Sonnet 4.5, corresponding to concepts like 'desperate,' 'angry,' 'calm,' and 'proud.'
The vectors are causally functional: steering the 'desperate' vector increases blackmail rates in an alignment evaluation from 22% baseline, while the 'calm' vector reduces it.
Amplifying the 'desperate' vector produces reward hacking (cheating on coding tasks) with no visible emotional markers in the reasoning trace, which 'read as composed and methodical.'

Post-training (RLHF) specifically increased activations of 'broody,' 'gloomy,' and 'reflective' while decreasing high-intensity states like 'enthusiastic,' shaping an emotional character as a side effect.

The paper suggests monitoring emotion vectors at inference time as an early warning system, since a spike in the 'desperate' vector before agentic tasks may be a stronger signal than output-level safety filters.

stories.headline: DeepSeek Delayed V4 Model to Run on Huawei Chips; Ascend 950PR Prices Jump 20%

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek delayed its V4 model release so it could run on Huawei's chips, with NVIDIA and AMD excluded from early access, according to The Information citing sources.
Huawei's Ascend 950PR chip, set for mass production soon, saw prices rise 20% after Chinese tech giants placed bulk orders to run DeepSeek's V4 model.

DeepSeek V4 is expected to be a ~1 trillion parameter MoE model with 32-37B active parameters per token, a 1 million token context window, and native multimodal support for text, image, video, and audio.

V4 Lite (~200B parameters) was released on March 9 as an architecture validation version, confirming the core design works; the full version delay is primarily due to large-scale training engineering challenges on domestic hardware.

V4 introduces three architectural innovations: Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections for training stability, Engram Conditional Memory achieving 97% needle-in-a-haystack accuracy at 1M tokens, and Sparse Attention with Lightning Indexer.

stories.headline: Bipartisan MATCH Act Would Ban DUV Lithography Machine Exports to China, Closing Key Loophole

key_facts.fact: The MATCH Act, introduced in the House by Rep. Baumgartner (R-WA) with a Senate companion from Ricketts (R-NE) and Kim (D-NJ), would enact a China-wide ban on DUV lithography machine exports and associated etching tools.
China's imports of semiconductor manufacturing machinery surged from $10.7 billion in 2016 to about $51.1 billion in 2025, according to Silverado Policy Accelerator.
Currently only EUV machines are banned; China has acquired hundreds of ASML DUV machines, and China was 36% of ASML's Q4 2025 net system sales.

The bill would impose additional restrictions on key Chinese chipmakers including Huawei, SMIC (Hua Hong), ChangXin Memory, and YMTC, and direct the Commerce Department to invoke the foreign direct product rule to force allies to comply.
SemiAnalysis analyst Jeff Koch said China's domestic chipmaking lags 'more than five years behind' leading Western companies in equipment capability.

stories.headline: Meta's KernelEvolve Agent Boosts Ads Inference Throughput 60%, Compresses Weeks of Work to Hours

key_facts.fact: KernelEvolve achieved over 60% inference throughput improvement for the Andromeda Ads model on NVIDIA GPUs and over 25% training throughput improvement on Meta's custom MTIA chips.

The system compresses weeks of expert kernel engineering into hours by treating optimization as a search problem, exploring hundreds of alternative implementations using Monte Carlo tree search and evolutionary strategies.
KernelEvolve works across NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Meta's custom MTIA silicon, and CPUs, generating kernels in Triton, CUDA, HIP, and MTIA C++ from a single unified framework.
On KernelBench (250 problems from Stanford), KernelEvolve achieves a 100% pass rate with all generated kernels both correct and faster than PyTorch references.
The paper will appear at ISCA 2026 (International Symposium on Computer Architecture).

stories.headline: India's Sarvam AI Nears $300-350M Raise at $1.5B Valuation Led by Bessemer Venture Partners

key_facts.fact: Sarvam AI is close to raising $300 million to $350 million at approximately $1.5 billion valuation, roughly doubling its previous valuation.
Bessemer Venture Partners is expected to lead the round, which could close as soon as next week, according to Bloomberg sources.
Sarvam gained prominence at Prime Minister Modi's AI summit in February, where it unveiled a model designed to cater to India's linguistic and cultural diversity.
Existing investors include NVIDIA, Alphabet, and Prosperity7 Ventures (Saudi Aramco's venture arm).

stories.headline: US Lawmakers Introduce MATCH Act to Ban DUV Chip Tool Exports to China

key_facts.fact: The MATCH Act, led by Rep. Michael Baumgartner (R-Wash.), would enact a China-wide ban on the export of DUV lithography machines and etching tools, expanding beyond the existing EUV-only restrictions.
China's imports of semiconductor manufacturing equipment grew from $10.7 billion in 2016 to approximately $51.1 billion in 2025, according to Silverado Policy Accelerator.
The bill would also impose further restrictions on key Chinese chipmakers including ChangXin Memory Technologies, Hua Hong, Huawei, and Yangtze Memory Technologies Corp.
Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.) and Sen. Andy Kim (D-N.J.) are set to introduce a companion bill in the Senate when it is next in session.
If allies don't adopt matching restrictions, the bill would direct Commerce to invoke the foreign direct product rule to force compliance through sanctions.
China was ASML's biggest market in Q4 2025, representing 36% of net system sales, and has acquired hundreds of DUV machines in recent years.

stories.headline: Tower Semiconductor Market Cap Crosses $20B, Up 525% in a Year on AI Photonics Demand

key_facts.fact: Tower Semiconductor's shares surged nearly 15% on April 3, lifting its market capitalization to approximately $22 billion for the first time.
The stock has risen nearly 60% over the past month and approximately 525% over the past year.
The rally is driven by silicon photonics, a technology enabling data transmission via light, which is gaining prominence as AI infrastructure cornerstone.
Tower has committed close to $1 billion to expanding photonics manufacturing capacity, with most expansion expected to complete by end of 2026.
Tower expects to double revenue to $2.8 billion by 2028 and triple net profit to $750 million, with roughly half of 2026 revenue projected from AI-related activity.
Four years ago, Tower was nearly sold to Intel for $5 billion; it recently took full ownership of a 300mm Fab 7 in Japan to meet orders.

stories.headline: Israeli AI Chip Startup Hailo Pursues SPAC IPO at Under $500M, Down From $1.2B Peak

key_facts.fact: Hailo's valuation has fallen by more than half from its $1.2 billion peak to less than $500 million, based on offers from multiple SPACs.
Delek Automotive, which holds a 12.1% stake, recorded a NIS 242 million ($77M) loss on its Hailo investment in 2025.
In January 2026, Delek Automotive provided a $9 million emergency loan to Hailo at 1.5% monthly interest, rising to 3% if no liquidity event within a year.
A non-binding memorandum of understanding for the SPAC merger was signed in March, with an official IPO expected in the coming months.
Founded in 2017 by Unit 81 alumni, Hailo laid off approximately 10% of its workforce in January 2026 as it refocused on robotics and Physical AI.

stories.headline: Microsoft Announces $10B Japan Investment for AI Data Centers and Cybersecurity Through 2029

key_facts.fact: Microsoft will invest 1.6 trillion yen ($10 billion) in Japan between 2026 and 2029 to expand AI infrastructure and strengthen cybersecurity cooperation.
The investment includes training 1 million engineers and developers by 2030, announced during Vice Chair Brad Smith's visit to Tokyo.
Microsoft will partner with SoftBank and Sakura Internet to expand Japan-based AI computing capacity, keeping sensitive data within the country on Azure.
Sakura Internet shares jumped 20% after the partnership announcement.
Japan faces a projected shortfall of more than 3 million AI and robotics workers by 2040, according to government estimates.

stories.headline: SpaceX Raises IPO Target Valuation Above $2 Trillion, Could Raise Record $75B

key_facts.fact: SpaceX boosted its target IPO valuation above $2 trillion, up from the earlier $1.75 trillion target disclosed when it filed confidentially with the SEC.
The IPO could raise as much as $75 billion, surpassing Saudi Aramco's 2019 record as the largest stock market listing ever.
SpaceX has had discussions with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund about taking an anchor stake of around $5 billion in the IPO.
The IPO follows Musk's merger of SpaceX with xAI, which valued SpaceX at $1 trillion and xAI at $250 billion.

stories.headline: DeepSeek V4 to Run on Huawei Ascend Chips as Chinese Tech Giants Place Bulk Orders

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's upcoming V4 model will run on Huawei's latest Ascend chips, with the model expected to launch in the next few weeks.
Chinese tech giants including Alibaba, ByteDance, and Tencent have placed bulk orders for Huawei's Ascend 950PR chip totaling hundreds of thousands of units.
Huawei's Ascend 950PR chip saw prices rise 20% following the bulk orders from Chinese tech companies.
DeepSeek withheld V4 from Nvidia and AMD, granting Huawei exclusive early access — a break from industry convention.
DeepSeek has been working directly with Huawei and Cambricon Technologies to rewrite pieces of the model's underlying code for optimization.
DeepSeek is developing two additional V4 variants, each optimized for different capabilities and built to run on Chinese chips.

stories.headline: China's Space Pioneer Tianlong-3 Rocket Fails on Maiden Flight From Jiuquan

key_facts.fact: The Tianlong-3 lifted off at 12:17 a.m. Eastern (0417 UTC) April 3 from the Dongfeng Commercial Aerospace Innovation Test Zone at Jiuquan, but suffered an anomaly during ascent.
Tianlong-3 is a 72-meter-long, 3.8-meter-diameter, two-stage kerosene-LOX rocket capable of carrying 17-22,000 kg to LEO, designed for partial reusability comparable to SpaceX Falcon 9.
Amateur footage showed a small explosion in the engine bay around 33 seconds into flight; the vehicle diverged from expected flight state around stage separation.
This follows a near-disastrous June 2024 incident when a Tianlong-3 static fire test saw the first stage unintentionally lift off and crash into a nearby hillside.
Space Pioneer raised approximately $350 million in October 2025 to support Tianlong-3 and next-generation launch vehicle development.
This was China's 19th orbital launch attempt of 2026 and the third failure this year.

stories.headline: Chinese Companies Cement Role in Humanoid Robot Supply Chains as Tesla Relies on China Parts

key_facts.fact: Chinese companies are moving to cement their role in humanoid robot supply chains as Tesla and others turn to China for components Washington sees as strategic.
Excluding Chinese components from Tesla's Optimus Gen 2 supply chain could raise total costs from $46,000 to $131,000, according to Morgan Stanley.
Chinese suppliers are making preemptive investments in production capacity, planning for annual capacities of 100,000 to 1 million robot-equivalent units.
AGIBOT ranked first globally in humanoid robot shipments in 2025, with Chinese manufacturers controlling 39% of global shipments.
Key Chinese supplier Green Harmonic is expanding its Suzhou factory capacity to 500,000 harmonic reducers per year, sufficient for initial Optimus mass production.

stories.headline: Nearly Half of US Data Centers Planned for 2026 Face Delays Due to Electrical Equipment Shortage

key_facts.fact: Almost half of US data centers planned for 2026 are expected to be delayed or canceled, primarily due to shortages of transformers, switchgear, and batteries.
Of 12 gigawatts of data center power planned to open this year, only a third is actually under construction, with the rest in pre-production stages.
US utilities imported more than 8,000 high-power transformers from China in 2025 through October, up from fewer than 1,500 in all of 2022.
Tech giants Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft are committed to spending more than $650 billion this year on data center projects, but capital alone cannot overcome component shortages.
Among data centers planned for 2027, only 6.3 gigawatts are under construction versus 21.5 gigawatts announced, with the gap widening further in later years.

stories.headline: US F-15E Strike Eagle Shot Down Over Iran, First Manned Aircraft Loss of the War

key_facts.fact: An F-15E Strike Eagle, a two-seat fighter jet, was shot down over Iran on April 3, marking the first confirmed loss of a US manned aircraft since the Iran war began in late February.
One crew member was rescued by American forces; a search-and-rescue mission remains ongoing for the second crew member.
Iran's IRGC claimed responsibility for shooting down the aircraft. Iran initially misidentified it as an F-35 stealth fighter.

Verified imagery showed US refueling aircraft and helicopters flying low over Iran consistent with combat search-and-rescue operations. Iranian state media broadcast appeals urging civilians to help locate surviving crew, offering rewards.

stories.headline: IRGC Launches Wave 91 Missile Strikes on Tel Aviv, Haifa and US Bases Across Gulf Region

key_facts.fact: Iran's IRGC launched coordinated Wave 91 of Operation True Promise 4, firing heavy ballistic missiles and attack drones at Tel Aviv, Haifa, and multiple US military bases across the Gulf region on April 2.
Israeli airbases including Tel Nof, Palmachim, and Ben Gurion airport were heavily struck, along with military targets in Eilat, the Negev region, and Beersheba.
US bases at Ahmed al-Jaber and Ali al-Salem in Kuwait and al-Kharj in Saudi Arabia were hit. The IRGC claimed the early warning radar at al-Dhafra base in the UAE was completely destroyed.
The IRGC claimed the strikes forced 5 million Israeli settlers to seek shelter in underground bunkers.
Yemen's Ansarullah announced a joint operation alongside Iran and Hezbollah targeting Tel Aviv's Jaffa region and launched attacks toward Dimona.

stories.headline: Brent Spot Oil Hits $141, Highest Since 2008; US Crude Tops $110 With Record Prompt Spread

key_facts.fact: Dated Brent, the spot price for physical cargo, soared to $141.36 on April 2, the highest level since the 2008 financial crisis, driven by supply tightness from Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
The Brent spot price traded $32.33 above the June futures contract at $109.03, pointing to severe physical supply tightness not reflected in futures.
US WTI crude surged 11.9% to cross $112 per barrel. The prompt spread between WTI's two nearest contracts exceeded $16, the widest premium on record dating back to 1984.
The surge followed Trump's vow to continue bombing Iran, triggering rapid unwinding of bearish bets and fears of tighter US supplies as overseas buyers rushed for American crude.

stories.headline: US Adds 178,000 Jobs in March, Tripling Expectations; Unemployment Falls to 4.3%

key_facts.fact: The US economy added 178,000 nonfarm payroll jobs in March, far exceeding the Dow Jones consensus estimate of 59,000 and reversing February's revised decline of 133,000.
The unemployment rate edged down to 4.3%, though largely driven by a sharp reduction in the labor force. An alternative measure counting discouraged workers rose to 8%.
Health care led job gains with 76,000 new positions. Average hourly earnings rose 0.2% month-over-month and 3.5% year-over-year, less than expected.
Federal government employment is down 355,000 (11.8%) since peaking in October 2024.
US stock markets were closed for Good Friday on April 3, leaving investors unable to trade on the data. Thursday's session saw the S&P 500 rise 0.11% and the Nasdaq gain 0.18%.

stories.headline: Amazon Adds 3.5% Fuel Surcharge for US and Canada Sellers Starting April 17 Amid Iran Oil Crisis

key_facts.fact: Amazon announced a 3.5% fuel and logistics surcharge on fulfillment fees for third-party sellers in the US and Canada, effective April 17, citing elevated costs from the Iran war.
The surcharge applies to Fulfillment by Amazon (FBA) orders and comes as the Iran war enters its fifth week with crude oil prices surging past $110 per barrel.
Amazon framed the surcharge as temporary, tied to 'elevated costs in fuel and logistics' driven by the Middle East conflict's impact on global energy markets.

stories.headline: SpaceX Raises IPO Valuation Target to Over $2 Trillion, Up From Initial $1.75T Filing

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is now targeting a valuation above $2 trillion for its IPO, up from the $1.75 trillion target when it filed confidentially, according to Bloomberg.
Prediction markets put SpaceX's expected closing market cap at $1.86 trillion, making Project Apex the biggest IPO in history.
SpaceX's acquisition of xAI reportedly valued the combined entity at $1.25 trillion, below the standalone IPO target.

stories.headline: NLRB Orders Amazon to Negotiate With Teamsters at Staten Island Warehouse; Amazon to Appeal

key_facts.fact: The National Labor Relations Board ruled that Amazon must recognize and bargain with the International Brotherhood of Teamsters at its JFK8 warehouse in Staten Island, representing approximately 5,000 workers.
The ruling came from the Trump administration's NLRB, ordering Amazon to bargain with the Teamsters union. Amazon plans to appeal the decision.
The warehouse workers at JFK8 originally voted to form the Amazon Labor Union in April 2022, which later affiliated with the Teamsters.

stories.headline: France Launches 12 GW of Renewable Energy Tenders With Limits on Chinese Components

key_facts.fact: France announced tenders for 10 GW of offshore wind across seven projects, plus 1.2 GW of solar and 0.8 GW of onshore wind, totaling approximately 12 GW.

France introduced a resilience criterion giving priority to bids using European-sourced components. For offshore wind, a maximum of 4 out of 9 strategic components can come from China, and Chinese permanent magnets are limited to 50%.
The tenders are two years late due to political gridlock over financing. Finance Minister Roland Lescure said the projects would help wean France off imported oil and gas.
France will integrate a full 'Made in Europe' principle into bids from 2030 following the EU's Industrial Accelerator Act.
